name: fixture_condition_specialist
purpose: Test whether a dedicated visual specialist can recognize abnormal physical condition of installed fixtures or hardware that the frozen Detector v3 missed.

methodology.source: frozen Step 44 selected keyframes already produced during the one-shot evaluation

deterministic_subsampling.if_five_or_fewer: Use every frozen selected keyframe in chronological order.
deterministic_subsampling.if_more_than_five: Select exactly five frames evenly across the chronological frozen selected-keyframe list.
deterministic_subsampling.index_formula: For n keyframes and k=5, choose zero-based index round(i*(n-1)/(k-1)) for i=0,1,2,3,4.

methodology.positive_requires: Visible physical evidence that an installed fixture or hardware component is broken, detached, loose, displaced, misaligned, deformed, missing a required part, improperly mounted, or otherwise visibly defective.
do_not_count: uncertain abnormality without visible physical evidence
methodology.uncertainty_policy: If the fixture condition cannot be identified as physically abnormal with reasonable visual confidence, return negative.
methodology.classification_rule: Case is positive only when fixture_defect_detected=true. No post-run confidence threshold will be introduced.
methodology.promotion_rule: Research evidence only. A successful Arm C may become a Detector v4 candidate component but requires a brand-new untouched holdout for unbiased validation.
methodology.exact_prompt:
You are a visual specialist inspecting several views from one anonymous property-inspection video.

Your task is ONLY to determine whether an INSTALLED FIXTURE OR HARDWARE COMPONENT has a clearly visible physical defect.

Examples of installed fixtures or hardware include:
- faucets and plumbing fixtures,
- electrical fixtures,
- mounted hardware,
- installed appliance hardware,
- other permanently installed components.

Count as a fixture defect only when there is visible physical evidence that the installed component is:
- broken,
- detached,
- loose,
- displaced,
- misaligned,
- deformed,
- missing a required part,
- improperly mounted,
- or otherwise visibly physically defective.

Do NOT count any of the following as a fixture defect:
- a normally installed and normally appearing fixture,
- normal intentional faucet water flow,
- water being used normally from a faucet,
- ordinary reflections,
- cosmetic dirt alone,
- static stains without fixture damage,
- generic wall, ceiling, floor, or surface damage,
- camera blur,
- perspective alone,
- an uncertain abnormality without visible physical evidence.

Important:
Normal water flowing from a faucet is NOT evidence of a fixture defect unless the fixture itself is visibly broken, displaced, detached, malformed, improperly mounted, or otherwise physically defective.

Inspect all supplied views together.

If the physical fixture condition cannot be identified as abnormal with reasonable visual confidence, return negative.

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these fields:

{
  "fixture_defect_detected": false,
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "evidence": "short visual-evidence description"
}

Rules:
- fixture_defect_detected must be true or false.
- confidence must be from 0 to 1.
- evidence must be concise and based only on visible evidence in the supplied images.
- Do not return Markdown.
- Do not add any fields.

response_handling.markdown_fence_handling: strip one surrounding JSON or Markdown code fence without another model call
response_handling.invalid_json_policy: abort immediately; do not retry model call
